dedupe_keys.name: transam open source transit asset management platform cambridge systematics

description: TransAM is an open-source platform for managing transportation assets, offered as a low-cost, licence-free alternative to proprietary asset management systems and designed for public transportation agencies. The README says it includes industry-standard models to forecast asset condition and replacement cycles, quantify capital needs, and develop and implement state-of-good-repair policies, and accommodates rolling stock, rail, facilities, shelters, signage, maintenance and communications equipment and computers. Functions are split into Ruby on Rails engines; the Core engine is the foundation for the others. Coverage: any agency asset base. Format and access: Ruby gem and source code. Licence and cost: MIT (copyright Cambridge Systematics, 2013 to 2019), free. Caveats: needs Rails development to deploy, and the licence dates suggest limited recent updates. It supports capacity planning and resilience work on asset condition and renewal. It relates to the National Transit Database in the catalogue.
